event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Sempra’s February 25 2022 filing discusses COVID-19 primarily as an ongoing, enterprise-wide source of operational and financial uncertainty.  Although management explicitly states that the pandemic has not yet produced a material hit to results, the risk language moves beyond boiler-plate by cataloguing concrete pressure points: altered work practices and the associated productivity drag, labour turnover, customer-protection measures that have already driven up bad-debt expense, and capital-markets volatility that has slowed spending plans.  These disclosures show both realised impacts (higher uncollectibles, market disruptions) and forward-looking threats (supply-chain strain, liquidity risk, compliance jeopardy).  Because the event window (March 2020-present) is well inside the 0-3-year “recent” band, the Time Decay Principle allows elevated severity scores.  Nevertheless, management’s statement that COVID-19 has not materially affected results to date, coupled with references to mitigation protocols, tempers the overall risk assessment.  Netting these factors, the pandemic constitutes a live, moderate-to-high emerging risk—significant enough to monitor closely, but not yet existential for Sempra.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has been materially impacting communities, supply chains, economies and markets around the world since March 2020.

components.reason: Links pandemic to broad systemic impacts, explicitly naming supply-chain disruption.
Statement is generic to global conditions, not company-specific.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges widespread, recent disruptions but does not yet tie them directly to Sempra’s own performance, yielding a modest risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: To date, the COVID-19 pandemic has not had a material impact on our results of operations.

components.reason: Expressly mitigates the severity by noting no material impact so far.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: This sentence is strongly mitigating, signalling limited realised damage, so it reduces the composite risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Conducting business with substantial modifications to employee travel and work locations and virtualization of certain business activities, which could result in increased employee turnover or absenteeism, decreased efficiency and productivity and other similar affects that could increase operating costs and jeopardize our ability to satisfy compliance requirements and sustain operations

components.reason: Identifies concrete operational changes (remote work, travel limits).
Details multiple potential impacts—labour shortages, productivity loss, higher costs, compliance risks.
Applies directly to Sempra’s ability to operate; near-term horizon.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific, company-level operational threats make this one of the stronger risk indicators, meriting a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Disruption in the capital markets, which has affected and could further affect liquidity, strategic initiatives and prospects, including in some cases a slowdown of planned capital spending

components.reason: Highlights direct impact already felt (‘has affected’) on liquidity.
Connects market turmoil to strategic and investment slow-downs.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows realised financial effects and plausible future constraints, producing a solid mid-high risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Customer-protection measures implemented by SDG&E and SoCalGas ... have collectively resulted in a reduction in payments from SDG&E and SoCalGas’ customers and an increase in uncollectible accounts that could become material and may not be fully recoverable

components.reason: Describes concrete, quantified-in-principle impact: reduced cash collections and rising bad-debt.
Warns that losses ‘may not be fully recoverable’, heightening severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: This sentence cites an already-incurred financial hit with potential materiality, justifying a high risk weighting.

evidence_list.snippet: Any of these impacts could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and/or prospects.

components.reason: Uses strong ‘material adverse effect’ phrasing to frame severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but emphatic statement that synthesises risk magnitude, adding modest weight to overall severity.
